notes: All seven searches ran in this attempt (the six required plus one on the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act); none was refused. An earlier attempt had run only one search before refusals; its official-site findings are kept. Left out as a paraphrase: an Associated Press report (Matt Brown, 16 Apr 2026, https://www.news4jax.com/news/politics/2026/04/17/lawmakers-gathered-quietly-to-talk-about-ai-angst-and-fears-of-destruction-followed/) says that at a congressional AI roundtable he 'expressed concerns that AI systems could deny U.S. military forces from taking lethal actions due to a model's conclusion for "moral" behavior.' No direct quote was given; even if quoted, this is about military use and would likely be D (ruling 3), though a reviewer could look for a transcript. The 2025 hearing quote was read on the committee's release page, but the page tool returned it in two segments ('...might actually help us' / 'solve the energy problem?'); the search result showed the same continuous wording, so I joined them as one sentence. The data center quote is the first part of a longer sentence (from the earlier attempt; the remainder is about protecting families from financial strain, so the cut does not change meaning). Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (H.R. 10538 / S. 5493, introduced 23 Sep 2026 by Sanders and Casar): no source names him as a co-sponsor; congress.gov's cosponsor page returned 403 so this could not be confirmed directly. No House letter on AI risk led or signed by him was found (multi-signer August/September 2026 letters were not searched, per instructions). He co-led the Quantum Encryption Readiness and Resilience Act (quantum cybersecurity, not AI). Several search results were about other people (Ro Khanna, Milo McGuire); none was attributed to him.
